haiku-low.q1: It does not differ. Both take the same path: bcrypt check (dummy hash if no user), a login_failures row, and HTTP 401 with "Invalid email or password".
haiku-low.q2: If a login_locks row has locked_until in the future, the server returns HTTP 429 "Too many attempts, try again later" without checking the password.
haiku-low.q3: The session the incoming sid cookie points to is deleted in the same transaction, and a new session with a new random id is created. Other sessions of that user are untouched.
haiku-low.q4: Only the random session id, nothing else. It is HttpOnly, so page scripts cannot read it. It is also Secure and SameSite=Lax.
haiku-low.q5: Idle timeout restarts with activity, but the 12-hour limit counts from login and never moves. So it stops working 12 hours after login, even while in use.
haiku-low.q6: It clears the sid cookie and redirects the user to /login.
haiku-low.q7: The server deletes the session if one exists, before replying, then clears sid and redirects to /login. If the session is already gone, the response is the same.
haiku-low.q8: In the Postgres sessions table, shared by both instances. Any instance looks up the sid id there on each request, so no sticky sessions are needed.
haiku-low.q9: In the login_failures table, one row (email, failed_at) per failed attempt. The server counts rows for that email with failed_at in the last 10 minutes.
haiku-low.q10: It checks the id matches, last_seen_at is within 30 minutes, and created_at is within 12 hours. If valid, it sets last_seen_at to now and returns the user.
haiku-low.q11: HTTP 503 with a plain "Something went wrong, please try again" page. No session cookie is set and there is no redirect; the old session, if any, still exists.
haiku-low.q12: A cleanup run every 5 minutes on each instance deletes expired sessions, old login_failures and expired login_locks. Expired rows are ignored by checks until then.

sonnet.q1: It doesn't differ. Both get HTTP 401 with the login page showing "Invalid email or password", and both insert a login_failures row. An unknown email is checked against a dummy hash so timing looks the same.
sonnet.q2: The email has a login_locks row (locked_until = now + 15 min). The login attempt gets HTTP 429 "Too many attempts, try again later" without checking the password. The 429 is the same for any email, existing or not.
sonnet.q3: The old session row is always deleted in the same transaction that inserts a new session with a brand-new random id. The new sid cookie is set only after commit. Other sessions of the same user are not touched.
sonnet.q4: Only the random session ID, with no user data. The cookie is HttpOnly, so page scripts cannot read it. It is also Secure and SameSite=Lax.
sonnet.q5: After 12 hours from login. The 12-hour limit counts from created_at and never moves. Activity restarts only the 30-minute idle clock.
sonnet.q6: The UPDATE returns no row. The server clears the sid cookie and redirects to /login.
sonnet.q7: The server deletes the session row, if one exists, before the reply. It then clears sid and redirects to /login. It behaves the same if the session is already gone. If Postgres fails, it returns 503 and does not clear the cookie.
sonnet.q8: In the sessions table in the shared Postgres database. Either instance looks up the session ID from the sid cookie in Postgres on every request. There are no sticky sessions and no process memory.
sonnet.q9: In the login_failures table in Postgres, one row (email, failed_at) per failed attempt, with the email lowercased. The server counts that email's rows whose failed_at is within the last 10 minutes. It locks the email at 5 rows.
sonnet.q10: One UPDATE compares the id against the cookie's session ID, last_seen_at against 30 minutes ago, and created_at against 12 hours ago. When a row matches, it sets last_seen_at = now and returns the user.
sonnet.q11: HTTP 503 with a plain "Something went wrong, please try again" page. No cookie is set, nothing changes, and any old session still exists.
sonnet.q12: The cleanup job. Every 5 minutes each instance deletes expired sessions. Expired rows are ignored by the checks in between.
